disposition_reason: Table 1 gives mean, median and IQR of lead, chromium, arsenic and mercury (ug/L) in 100 raw cow milk samples from 25 farms in five zones of Atlantico, Colombia; text adds seasonal means.

study.origin: 25 cattle farms in five zones of the Department of Atlantico, Caribbean Colombia
study.market: not market; bulk storage tanks after morning milking

period.as_reported: dry season December 2018-February 2019; rainy season September-November 2019

study.method: Pb and Cr by graphite furnace AAS (Thermo ICE 3500), As by HG-AFS, Hg by direct mercury analyzer (EPA 7470), after HNO3/HCl microwave digestion of 5 mL
study.qa: standard addition recoveries 88-94%, CV below 3.5%; no CRM reported

controls.outcome: Lead mean 1.10 (dry) vs 9.71 ug/L (rainy); Pb, Cr and As significantly higher in the rainy season (p < 0.001); Hg higher in the dry season (not significant)

unresolved: The text says lead in milk 'from both dairy farms and collection centers' exceeded the EU 20 ug/L limit, but every reported lead statistic is below 10 ug/L, and no collection-center samples are described.
Abstract factors (Pb x20, Cr x44, As x3, Hg x0.5) do not match the text's ninefold lead change.
Zone 2 arsenic mean in text (3.97 ug/L) conflicts with Table 1 (2.43).
Zone sample sizes are not given (20 per zone if equal).
Season-by-zone values exist only in figures (Fig. 2, Fig. 3); not read.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU maximum level for lead in milk (Regulation (EU) 2023/915) cited
